subject: Graphing large data frames in ggplot2

messages.author: ff774d4d8911959e
messages.subject: Graphing large data frames in ggplot2
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to make a complex grid of scatterplots from a large data
frame (ie NGS sequencing data and a data.frame with 112,000 rows)
using the excellent faceting capability of ggplot2, but the R Gui
doesn't like this, and tells me

Error: cannot allocate vector of size 684.0 Mb

Yikes, I think I need more RAM to do my graphics in ggplot2. How do I
do this?

Thanks for any help!!

Elena

messages.author: 3454c1b8e3e4b559
messages.subject: AW: Graphing large data frames in ggplot2
parts:
Elena,

two possibilities:
- either go and buy a few GB of RAM (and make sure you have a 64 bit R running), or (and?)
- try to calculate summary statistics beforehand and without the help of ggplot.

In a scatterplot of >1e5 points you're anyways not likely to see much. But a hexbin 2d histogram could be a good start, and you can do that with small binwidth. You can find an elaborate example here:
https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/Case-Study%3A-Raman-Spectroscopic-Grading-of-Gliomas

Claudia
